summary: The artifacts-decide half of this item is real and has teeth. I drove all five declared falsifications in a scratch copy, proved each landed with a diff, and AC1, AC2, AC3 and AC4 each reddened the row their own field names. AC5 is REFUTED: its declared mutation is 'hand-list the artifact patterns instead of taking them from verdict_corpus', and applied faithfully, with the same two literal values, in both mirrors, the suite is 43 passed 0 failed and the FULL gate is GREEN at 4530 passed 0 failed. The row reds only when the hand-list ALSO changes a value, which is a different defect already caught by AC1 and AC3, so the check cannot detect the hand-kept copy the criterion exists to forbid. Its text is also false about the code twice: verdict_corpus declares FOUR corpus patterns and the suite compares against a two-element set hand-spelled IN THE SUITE, so the second spelling moved rather than disappeared; and the live row says it asserts equality 'against that module rather than recomputed here' while recomputing the spec-id extraction inline as split('/')[1] instead of calling spec_id_for_verdict. Worse for the item's purpose than any single AC, and measured on the live tree: the shipped reader gives the wrong answer about THIS repository. `python3 .veldo/work_state.py report` prints two lines, '142 done, 0 unconcluded, 69 queued' and the stand-down, and inside that 69 sit 13 items whose proof manifest is ON DISK, including all twelve VELDO specs of this migration. Work that was built and is awaiting a verdict is reported QUEUED, indistinguishable from work nobody started, with no path printed. Create one run folder and the same report turns into 144 lines of which 142 say 'UNRECORDED ... work a dead session left behind' about specs that landed months ago. The 69 is not the 'ready, unclaimed' the taxonomy declares either: 33 of those specs are status shipped, 4 draft, 1 blocked, because ready_specs filters nothing despite a docstring that says it returns specs 'whose spec file declares status ready'. And that same header states '0 unconcluded' while the run half has stood down, which is the confident zero AC4 forbids, in the one count its suite never checks. SEPARATE FROM THIS ITEM, AND URGENT: the gate is RED at this commit right now, and not because of VELDO-0002. WARP-0727 AC1 in scripts/suites/13_warp_0623_codified_live.py asserts over the LIVE repository that the git-TRACKED verdict set EQUALS the ON-DISK verdict set, so every L2 reviewer who writes an untracked verdict-l2.json reds the gate; ten such files already exist on disk (170 tracked against 180 on disk), while .veldo/validate.py's own domain check declares untracked 'the one legitimate reason ... so it is not red'. FINDINGS SHAPE NOTE: the L2 template prescribes severity blocker|major|minor, which .veldo/validate.py rejects (list-shaped findings entries need severity blocking|note), so each entry carries a legal severity plus the template's value in `level`, the convention proof/VELDO-0010/verdict-l2.json already used.

criteria.note: DROVE THE DECLARED FALSIFICATION. In a scratch copy I replaced `is_done = concluded(entry)` with `is_done = any(r.get('run_said') == 'done' for r in claimed.get(sid, []))`, proved it landed by diff, and the row the field names reddened: 'AC1: a run recording status DONE for a spec with NO proof bundle is reported UNCONCLUDED', together with the AC1 negative control, 36 passed 6 failed against a 43/0 baseline. Read the code: concluded() requires BOTH verdict_corpus.VERDICT_PATTERN and MANIFEST_PATTERN entries, so nothing in the run half can set DONE, and the negative control (bundle on disk, no run folder anywhere) proves the run half cannot veto the artifact half. The half-written-bundle row is real too. WITHIN THE AC'S LETTER BUT WORTH KNOWING: DONE is a pure filesystem predicate. I built fixtures where a bundle whose verdict.json says {'verdict': 'fail'} is reported DONE, and where a proof directory that is not a spec at all (proof/scratch-notes/) is reported DONE and counted. This very verdict, written by a reviewer failing the item, flips VELDO-0002 from queued to done: 143 done, measured. The AC says 'proof bundle and verdict exist on disk, and for no other reason', so this is the letter working as written rather than a refutation.

DROVE THE DECLARED FALSIFICATION. I inserted `return "running", age` immediately after the age computation in liveness(), proved it landed by diff, and three rows reddened including the one the field names ('a run whose heartbeat is 15 hours old is LIVENESS_UNCONFIRMED and carries THE AGE') plus the negative control, 40 passed 3 failed. The age is genuinely the product: the stale fixture asserts 53000 < age < 55000 rather than a word, the no-heartbeat fixture asserts age is None and the printed line says 'no heartbeat ever recorded', and the 1-second fixture reports active, so UNCONFIRMED is a measurement and not the module's only answer. THREE WEAKNESSES I MEASURED IN THE SAME BRANCH, filed as F6 and F7, none of which contradicts this criterion's own sentence: a run recording status 'aborted' is reported with liveness 'run_recorded_done' and the printed line never carries run_said, so the only word an operator reads about an aborted run is 'done'; a heartbeat stamped three hours in the FUTURE is clamped to age 0 and printed 'active, last heartbeat 0s ago'; and a heartbeat written 2 seconds ago in an offset-bearing ISO spelling fails the single strptime format and is printed 'no heartbeat ever recorded', which this module's own docstring defines as liveness never having been confirmed once.

DROVE THE DECLARED FALSIFICATION. I deleted the entire `elif item['state'] == DONE and not item['claims'] and not rep['runs_stood_down']` branch, proved it landed by diff, and the named UNRECORDED row reddened, 40 passed 2 failed (the second red is AC4's negative control raising IndexError, correctly surfaced as a named row by the _ws_block wrapper instead of silently truncating the fragment). Both directions exist, they are separate lists, and the negative control holds: the spec that is both claimed and concluded appears in neither. TWO LIMITS I MEASURED, filed as F2 and F3. First, the UNRECORDED direction is gated on `not rep['runs_stood_down']` and this repository has no run registry (.git/veldo does not exist), so on the live tree the direction that exists for the 2026-08-10 shape is structurally inert and reports 0. Second, when I created a single run folder to exercise it, 142 specs that landed long ago immediately became 'UNRECORDED ... finished artifacts that NO run ever claimed - work a dead session left behind', because a registry that has never claimed them cannot distinguish 'completed off the record last night' from 'completed a year before the registry existed'. A half-written bundle nobody claimed, which is what a session dying mid-write leaves, appears in NEITHER list and gets no printed line at all. AC3's text is about a bundle that 'COMPLETED off the record', so its letter holds; both gaps are against the item's purpose.

DROVE THE DECLARED FALSIFICATION. I replaced `rep['runs_standdown_reason'] = STANDDOWN_NO_REGISTRY` with `rep['runs_stood_down'] = False`, proved it landed by diff, and two rows reddened including the one the field names, 41 passed 2 failed. The stand-down is real and well built: it carries a reason that distinguishes 'no run has ever recorded itself here' from 'no run is in flight', the corpus half still answers, the key shape is identical either way (asserted against REPORT_KEYS in both directions), and the negative control with a registry present does not stand down. THE HEADLINE CLAIM IS NOT FULLY TRUE, filed as F5: the same report prints '0 unconcluded' in its first line while the run half has stood down, and UNCONCLUDED is defined as 'a run claimed it and no artifact concludes it', a purely registry-derived predicate. The suite refuses exactly this reasoning for the sibling state in the same fixture, in these words: 'with the run half stood down NOTHING is called UNRECORDED, because being unclaimed cannot be measured against a registry that does not exist. Asserting it here would be the same confident zero pointing the other way'. It then never looks at counts['unconcluded'] or at counts['queued'], which depends on the same unmeasurable predicate. On the live tree the shipped CLI prints '142 done, 0 unconcluded, 69 queued' one line above 'run half STOOD DOWN ... answers nothing'.

THE DECLARED FALSIFICATION DOES NOT FALSIFY IT. The field says: hand-list the artifact patterns the corpus half walks instead of taking them from verdict_corpus. I did exactly that with the values unchanged, `return ('verdict*.json', 'manifest.json')` replacing the two-line delegation, in BOTH .veldo/work_state.py and engine/.veldo/work_state.py so the template-sync mirror check could not stand in for the criterion. The diff proves it landed and the two mirrors are byte-identical. The suite is 43 passed, 0 failed, character for character the baseline, and `bash scripts/verify.sh` reports 'selftest: 4530 passed, 0 failed', 'template sync: pass (122 pair(s) compared)' and 'GATE: GREEN'. The row reds only when the hand-list ALSO changes a value: `verdict.json` for `verdict*.json` gives 34 passed 8 failed, which is the run proof/VELDO-0002/driven-falsifications.txt recorded as 'AC5 hand-listed-patterns HAS TEETH'. A wrong pattern is a different defect, already caught by AC1's and AC3's rows, and value equality between two reads of the same constants cannot detect a copy that copies correctly, which is the entire defect class this criterion names. TWO FALSE STATEMENTS ABOUT THE CODE ON TOP OF THAT. (1) 'SET EQUALITY between the patterns this reader walks and the patterns that module declares': verdict_corpus declares FOUR corpus patterns (VERDICT_PATTERN, DESIGN_VERDICT_PATTERN, APPROVAL_PATTERN, MANIFEST_PATTERN, .veldo/verdict_corpus.py:136-139) and the suite compares against `{_WS_VC.VERDICT_PATTERN, _WS_VC.MANIFEST_PATTERN}`, a two-element set hand-spelled in the suite, so the second spelling of 'which patterns matter' moved from the module into its test. (2) the live row's own message says it is 'asserted as set equality against that module rather than recomputed here' while recomputing the spec-id extraction inline as `_ws_v.split('/')[1]` instead of calling `_WS_VC.spec_id_for_verdict`, which is one shape read in two places, the thing this criterion exists to forbid. WHAT IS GOOD HERE, stated so it is not lost: the live row is genuine set equality with no cardinality pin and no non-empty requirement, and I confirmed by adding a fresh bundle that both sides move together, so it does not redden on first real use.

findings.text: AC5's check cannot fail for the defect it names. Its declared falsification, hand-listing the corpus patterns in .veldo/work_state.py instead of taking them from verdict_corpus, leaves the suite AND the whole gate green whenever the hand-list preserves the current values, which is exactly what a hand-kept copy looks like on the day it is written. The assertion is value equality between two reads of the same two constants, so it can only catch a WRONG pattern, never a duplicated spelling; the drift it exists to prevent would arrive the day verdict_corpus renames a pattern, as invisibly as the two prior divergences the criterion cites. The criterion also misstates the code: verdict_corpus declares four corpus patterns, and the 'declared' set the suite measures against is a two-element literal written inside the suite, so the second spelling was relocated rather than removed.
findings.evidence: Scratch copy of the tree at .../scratchpad/rev-VELDO-0002. Replaced in BOTH mirrors: `vc = _sibling("verdict_corpus") / return (vc.VERDICT_PATTERN, vc.MANIFEST_PATTERN)` became `return ("verdict*.json", "manifest.json")`. Proof it landed: `diff .veldo/work_state.py engine/.veldo/work_state.py` identical, `grep -n MUTATION` shows line 85 in both files. `python3 scripts/selftest.py --suite 19_veldo_0002_work_state` prints '19_veldo_0002_work_state 17 passed' and 'selftest (PARTIAL, 1 of 34 suites): 43 passed, 0 failed' with zero SELFTEST FAIL lines, identical to the pre-mutation baseline. `bash scripts/verify.sh` prints 'selftest: 4530 passed, 0 failed', 'template sync: pass (122 pair(s) compared, 6 declared per-repo, 131 engine-only)' and 'GATE: GREEN (dda45bff3e86fb336f5899f37ed6678a42ce06b6)'. The value-changing variant `return ("verdict.json", "manifest.json")` reds 8 rows (34 passed, 8 failed). Pattern constants at .veldo/verdict_corpus.py:136-139; the suite's comparison at scripts/suites/19_veldo_0002_work_state.py:284.

findings.text: On the live tree the reader answers its own scenario wrongly. A proof bundle is written in two stages, the producer's manifest and then a reviewer's verdict, so every item that is BUILT and awaiting review has a manifest and no verdict. That state is reported QUEUED, the same bucket as work nobody has started, and report_lines prints no line and no path for a queued item. Thirteen items in this repository are in it, including all twelve VELDO specs of this migration; VELDO-0002 itself, whose manifest records 5 of 5 criteria passed, is reported queued. The UNRECORDED direction that would have named them is gated on a run registry that does not exist here, so the entire report an operator gets after a loss is two lines: a count and a stand-down. PLAN-0018's measure for this item is 'kill a session mid-flight, start a fresh one, ask what is done, and get the right answer without anyone grepping worktrees'; a fresh session asking today is told the twelve built items are queued.
findings.evidence: `cd /home/dmitry/projects/veldo && python3 .veldo/work_state.py report` at HEAD prints exactly two lines: 'work state: 142 done, 0 unconcluded, 69 queued (artifacts decide done, never a run's own word)' and '  run half STOOD DOWN, recorded rather than reported as zero: no run registry exists under the git common dir...'. `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` is .git and `ls .git/veldo` is 'No such file or directory'. Enumerating rep['items'] over the live tree: 69 queued, 13 of which carry artifacts on disk, being proof/VELDO-0001/manifest.json through proof/VELDO-0012/manifest.json. Fixture confirmation: a ready spec with only manifest.json and no run claiming it gives state 'queued', unrecorded [], unconcluded [], and no report line mentioning it.
findings.criterion: AC3, and the item's stated measure

findings.text: Using the run registry once turns the report into 142 false alarms. UNRECORDED means 'artifacts exist that no run ever claimed', and the printed line calls it 'work a dead session left behind'. A registry that is fresh, or that was flattened at migration as this one was, has claimed nothing, so the first run folder to appear makes every historically landed spec qualify. I created one run folder and the report went from 2 lines to 144, of which 142 are UNRECORDED lines naming specs that landed long ago; the single genuinely interesting line, the stale run, is line 2 and is then buried. The organ whose stated product is 'a path to look at' hands the operator 142 paths, all wrong. This does not red the gate, because the suite's live row deliberately points at a nonexistent runs root, so no assertion covers the report's behaviour once a registry exists.
findings.evidence: In the scratch copy: created .git/veldo/runs/run-l2probe with meta.json and state.json (status running, heartbeat 40000s old). `python3 .veldo/work_state.py report | wc -l` is 144 and `grep -c UNRECORDED` is 142; counts are {'done': 143, 'queued': 68, 'unconcluded': 0, 'unrecorded': 142}. Sample lines: 'UNRECORDED WARP-0100: finished artifacts that NO run ever claimed - proof/WARP-0100/manifest.json, ...', likewise WARP-0101, WARP-0102, WARP-0103. Gating expression at .veldo/work_state.py:229; the suite's live row pins runs_root to ROOT/'no-such-runs-root-for-this-row' at scripts/suites/19_veldo_0002_work_state.py:290.

findings.text: QUEUED is not 'ready, unclaimed' as the spec's error taxonomy declares, and the docstring of the function that feeds it claims a filter the code does not have. ready_specs() is documented as 'Spec ids whose spec file declares status ready' but returns EVERY spec in specs/ with whatever status it declares, and work_report buckets all of them as QUEUED when they have no complete bundle. The queued number an operator acts on therefore mixes shipped, draft and blocked specs with genuinely ready ones, and the printed report carries no status beside it.
findings.evidence: Live tree, tabulating rep['items'] by spec_status within the queued bucket: {'ready': 31, 'shipped': 33, 'blocked': 1, 'draft': 4} out of 69. Fixture: a spec declaring `status: draft` with no artifacts is reported state 'queued', spec_status 'draft'. `WS.ready_specs()` over a fixture of three specs declaring draft, ready and superseded returns all three. Docstring at .veldo/work_state.py:111-115, use at :211-214.

findings.text: A confident zero survives inside the criterion that forbids confident zeros. With the run half stood down, work_report still reports counts['unconcluded'] = 0 and report_lines prints it in the headline, although UNCONCLUDED is defined entirely by a registry claim and is therefore unmeasurable when no registry exists. The suite reasons the opposite way about the sibling state in the same fixture, refusing to fill UNRECORDED 'because being unclaimed cannot be measured against a registry that does not exist', and then never looks at the unconcluded count or at QUEUED, which rests on the same predicate. So the report's first line, the line an operator reads first, states a zero derived from the half that just announced it answers nothing.
findings.evidence: Live tree: `python3 .veldo/work_state.py report` line 1 is 'work state: 142 done, 0 unconcluded, 69 queued' and line 2 is the stand-down. Fixture with with_registry=False and one ready spec: counts {'done': 0, 'unconcluded': 0, 'queued': 1, 'unrecorded': 0}. The suite's asymmetric rows are at scripts/suites/19_veldo_0002_work_state.py:251-254; the counts are built at .veldo/work_state.py:177-179 and printed at :239-240.

findings.text: An ABORTED run is reported with the word 'done'. liveness() maps status 'done' and status 'aborted' to the same answer, LIVENESS_DONE = 'run_recorded_done', and report_lines prints only that word, so run_said, which still carries 'aborted' in the JSON, never reaches the human-readable report. An operator reading the line for a run that aborted 25 hours ago is handed the reassuring word for the opposite fact, in a module whose stated discipline is that states are never collapsed.
findings.evidence: Fixture: run status 'aborted', heartbeat 90000s old. Result: liveness 'run_recorded_done', run_said 'aborted', item state 'unconcluded'; printed line 'run run-abort spec WARP-8004: run_recorded_done, last heartbeat 90000s ago. Started ... Look in ...'. Code at .veldo/work_state.py:163-164 and :244-249.

findings.text: The heartbeat age, which this item calls its product, has two spellings that print the wrong fact. _heartbeat_age accepts exactly one format, '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ', and returns None for anything else, and report_lines renders None as 'no heartbeat ever recorded', which the module's docstring explicitly defines as liveness never having been confirmed once. A registry entry stamped two seconds ago in an offset-bearing ISO spelling therefore prints the strongest available negative statement about a live run. In the other direction the age is clamped with max(0, ...), so a future-dated stamp, which is what clock skew across the machines this registry is shared between produces, prints 'active, last heartbeat 0s ago', the most reassuring line the report can emit, from a clock it cannot verify.
findings.evidence: Fixture with heartbeat_at '2026-08-12T11:32:06+00:00' written 2 seconds before the read: age None, liveness LIVENESS_UNCONFIRMED, printed line 'run r1 spec WARP-8100: LIVENESS_UNCONFIRMED, no heartbeat ever recorded'. Fixture with a heartbeat three hours in the future: age 0, liveness 'active', printed line 'active, last heartbeat 0s ago'. Code at .veldo/work_state.py:141-152.

findings.text: NOT VELDO-0002's DEFECT, REPORTED BECAUSE IT IS LIVE NOW: the gate is RED at this commit, and the review process itself is what reds it. WARP-0727 AC1 in scripts/suites/13_warp_0623_codified_live.py asserts over the live repository that the git-TRACKED verdict set EQUALS the ON-DISK verdict set. Every L2 reviewer writes proof/<SPEC>/verdict-l2.json and nobody commits it during the review, so each such artifact breaks the equality; ten already exist on disk. This is the shape the review brief warns about, a live-state assertion whose set must be empty reddening the first time somebody uses the feature, and .veldo/validate.py's own domain check disagrees with it in writing: untracked is 'the one legitimate reason and is expected (an author validating before committing), so it is not red'. One of the two is wrong, and today it is the selftest that fires.
findings.evidence: Read-only over /home/dmitry/projects/veldo at HEAD: events.tracked_verdicts(repo_root=ROOT) returns 170 paths, validate._corpus(VERDICT_PATTERN) returns 180, tracked_not_disk is empty and disk_not_tracked is proof/VELDO-0001, 0003, 0004, 0005, 0006, 0008, 0009, 0010, 0011, 0012 verdict-l2.json, so the equality WARP-0727 AC1 requires is False. Independently reproduced in the scratch copy by adding one untracked verdict-l2.json: `bash scripts/verify.sh` prints 'SELFTEST FAIL: WARP-0727 AC1: THE ENTITLEMENT DOMAIN AND THE VALIDATED SET ARE ONE ENUMERATION...', 'selftest: 4529 passed, 1 failed' and 'GATE: RED', where the same tree without that file is GREEN at 4530. Assertion at scripts/suites/13_warp_0623_codified_live.py:2568-2574 (`_v27_domain_paths == _v27_validated`); the contradicting doctrine at .veldo/validate_checks.py:79-81.

findings.text: NOT VELDO-0002's DEFECT: the L2 verdict shape this review was handed and the shipped validator disagree, so writing the artifact exactly as prescribed reds the contracts stage on top of everything else. The template declares findings entries with severity blocker|major|minor; .veldo/validate.py requires list-shaped findings entries to carry severity blocking|note. Every reviewer has to discover this and work around it, as proof/VELDO-0010/verdict-l2.json did by carrying a legal severity plus a separate `level` key, which is what this file does too.
findings.evidence: Scratch copy: wrote proof/VELDO-0002/verdict-l2.json with a findings entry of severity 'blocker'. `python3 .veldo/validate.py all` printed 'proof/VELDO-0002/verdict-l2.json: list-shaped findings entries need severity blocking|note and text' and 'veldo contracts: 1 problem(s)', exit 1; removing the file returned exit 0. Contract at .veldo/validate.py:274-277.
